pattern-selector.why: WP2 changes this skill's own gate and ships its PoEAA page registry, so the catalog it chooses from is checked for correct citations, not just present ones.
pattern-selector.what: added references/poeaa-registry.json (51 rows, one owner of page facts) and scripts/poeaa-registry.mjs; extended check-catalog-completeness.mjs to compare every PoEAA citation with the registry and to check coverage; updated SKILL.md and the catalog header.
quotes: chooses from can be kept honest, and it must be, because every other skill here ships a gate.

architectural-decision-records.why: making a committed registry the single owner of PoEAA page facts, shared by the catalog gate and the edit-time plan check, and adding Scenario Outline support to the BDD runner are lasting decisions with rejected alternatives.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0106 (four considered options, how the registry was built, consequences and limits); check_adr.sh passes.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the WP2 scenarios graduate from docs/design into features/ with real step definitions, and the runner needed Scenario Outline support to execute them.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: moved citation-gate.feature into features/pattern-selector/, graduated the three WP2 record scenarios into features/always-on/pattern-decision-citations.feature, wrote step files that drive the real gate and plan check, added outline support to bdd-run.mjs, regenerated the index, appended the coverage log; bdd-run 135 runs pass and check-bdd-executed covers 114 scenarios.
quotes: files and go green while no behavior was ever exercised

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the gate, the registry reader, the plan check, and the runner each need unit tests at the layer that owns the behavior, beyond the BDD scenarios.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: extended test/pattern-catalog.test.mjs (PoEAA cases, fitness test with --also-scan), added test/poeaa-registry.test.mjs (validator, 15 pinned pages, matching), extended test/check-task-plan.test.mjs and test/bdd-run.test.mjs; wired the new file into npm test.
quotes: checker that decides pass or fail but is itself wrong

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the audit's core finding was a gate that could not detect a wrong page; the replacement must be proven to detect.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: marked the single page comparison as the mutation target; with it replaced by a no-op, 17 catalog tests fail (run by hand and by the poeaa-gate-test-discriminates scenario on every BDD run); planted an in-order registry typo (Repository 320) and the pinned-page test fails.
quotes: A test that runs the check but asserts nothing tied to detection would let a broken check ship green.

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR and the PR make factual claims about the registry's source and the gate's detection, each needing an evidence state and a source.
skeptical-audit.what: cross-checked all 51 registry rows against the audit appendix and the book's table of contents by script (0 mismatches); tagged ADR claims; claim-lint --strict clean on ADR-0106.
quotes: Before you hit send, scan your own draft for the banned moves above.

judge-arch.why: the change adds a module, extends two gates and a hook-side checker, so it gets a fresh-context review recorded in the log before it is called done.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent review over every changed file and the four questions; fixed all 7 findings (3 high, 3 med, 1 low) in the same change with a regression test each; recorded the review in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: Review from a blank slate, never from the conversation that wrote the code.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the design keeps one owner for page facts and one reader shared by two callers, instead of a second copy in the plan check.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept the registry as data with one reader module (three callers: the gate, the plan check, the tests); no framework or abstraction beyond that.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: check-task-plan.mjs now imports code from the installed skills directory, which is a trust decision: tampering with that file would run code in the hook.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: threat: tampering (STRIDE T) with pattern-selector/scripts/poeaa-registry.mjs under --skills-dir. Countermeasures: the path is fixed (skills dir plus two constant segments, no input-derived parts); the file has the same trust as the hook scripts from the same install; the registry is read with JSON.parse, never evaluated; a present but unreadable or invalid registry is held (fail closed). Recorded in ADR-0106 Consequences.
quotes: A threat with no countermeasure is a vulnerability, not a decision.

arch-encode.why: the no-dash house rule is checkable, so the new ADR, features, step files, and registry test are added to the mechanical gate.
arch-encode.what: added ADR-0106, features/pattern-selector, and the new feature and step files to house-style-no-em-dash; npm run check:architecture exits 0. (Correction to the first receipt line for this change: test/poeaa-registry.test.mjs was also listed, but the gate never scans test folders, so arch-gate-wired caught the dead entry and it was removed.)
quotes: A rule that can be mechanical should be.

release-deployment-safety.why: no service is deployed or migrated; the skills mirror picks up the registry at the v1.4 release refresh (spec R10.1), and an older mirror is reported not-assessed rather than blocked.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data is stored, moved, or deleted.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no service, endpoint, or production system is added or changed.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI is rendered or changed.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing flow or plain-language document is added; the design README and ADR are maintainer docs.
